item.title: Zamfara: Jaji wins APC rerun primary by 26,646 votes
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau A member representing Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) fresh primary election for the constituency with a landslide victory. Jaji emerged winner of the rerun primary conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, polling 26,646 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, who scored 713 votes. The third aspirant, Musa Zubairu, polled no votes. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the Kaura-Namoda/Birnin Magaji fresh primary, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the constituency’s collation centre in Kaura-Namoda. Giving a breakdown of the exercise, Idris said the constituency had 42,266 registered party members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited to vote, while 27,359 votes were cast. In the results announced, Jaji scored 14,264 votes in Kaura-Namoda Local Government Area, against Dangaladima’s 465 votes, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji Local Government Area, Jaji polled 12,382 votes, while Dangaladima secured 248 votes. Zubairu again scored zero. Declaring the result, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC constitution and the party’s guidelines, and was therefore returned as the winner of the fresh primary. The rerun followed a suit filed by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court, Abuja, which nullified Jaji’s earlier nomination and ordered the party to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The APC national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the rerun, in compliance with the court’s order. item.title: APC chieftain to DSS: Scrutinise Dino Melaye’s statements
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi An All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain and loyalist of President Bola Tinubu, Khamis Musa Darazo, has urged the Department of State Services (DSS) and other security agencies to scrutinise recent statements attributed to former Kogi West Senator, Dino Melaye, concerning the 2027 general elections. Darazo, who made the call while speaking with journalists in Bauchi on Thursday, said the move was necessary to safeguard national security and prevent political utterances capable of heightening tension or creating unnecessary apprehension among Nigerians. He, however, cautioned that his call should not be interpreted as an attempt to intimidate opposition politicians or suppress democratic freedoms, stressing that democracy accommodates criticism, disagreement and healthy political competition. According to him, political leaders must recognise the responsibility that comes with public statements, particularly as the country approaches another election cycle. “This is not about persecution, intimidation or silencing the opposition. It is about responsibility. If a statement made by a prominent political actor has generated legitimate security concerns, the authorities have every right to seek clarification and establish the facts,” he said. Darazo maintained that security agencies must apply the law fairly, irrespective of political affiliation, warning against the use of national security as a partisan instrument. He also urged Melaye and other political leaders to exercise restraint in their public statements, saying Nigeria could not afford another atmosphere of political tension, fear and confrontation ahead of the 2027 elections. “Political disagreement is normal in a democracy. What is unacceptable is allowing political competition to gradually become a source of tension among citizens. We should sell our ideas, present our records and persuade Nigerians rather than create unnecessary anxiety,” he added. The APC chieftain challenged opposition politicians to focus their campaigns on policies, programmes, leadership capacity and verifiable records rather than provocative statements capable of distracting attention from issues affecting Nigerians. He said supporters of President Tinubu were prepared for the 2027 political contest and would continue to defend the administration based on its policies, achievements and Renewed Hope Agenda. “We are not afraid of opposition. We welcome competition. But competition must be democratic, peaceful and issue-based. President Tinubu will be judged by Nigerians based on his record, just as every opposition politician will be judged by the people based on what they offer,” Darazo said. He called on the DSS and other relevant security institutions to remain professional, impartial and guided by the law in handling politically sensitive matters. item.title: 2027: S’west monarchs back southern presidency, endorse Tinubu, support state police
item.description: …reject fuel subsidy return, urge peaceful elections, commend new military formations in Oyo, Ekiti By Adeola Badru Traditional rulers from across the South-West have endorsed the continuation of the presidency in Southern Nigeria beyond the 2027 general elections, declaring that sustaining the principle of power rotation is critical to national unity, political stability, equity and inclusiveness. The monarchs also reaffirmed their unwavering support for President Bola Tinubu and his administration while backing the proposed establishment of state police as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s security architecture. These were among the major resolutions reached at a meeting of the South-West Council of Obas and Traditional Rulers held at the Aafin Olubadan, Oke Aremo, Ibadan, Oyo State, on Wednesday. The meeting, which brought together prominent traditional rulers from the six South-West states, also endorsed the Federal Government’s position against the reintroduction of fuel subsidy, called for peaceful and credible elections in 2027, and urged greater collaboration among Nigeria’s geopolitical regions. In a communiqué issued and read by the Alake of Egbaland, Oba Adedotun Gbadebo, at the end of the meeting, said the rotational presidency arrangement had contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness and national cohesion, stressing that the arrangement should be sustained in the next electoral cycle. The Council declared, “The principle of rotational presidency has, over the years, contributed significantly to political stability, inclusiveness, and national cohesion across Nigeria.” “In the interest of fairness, equity, and the continued strengthening of national unity, the Council expressed the view that the rotational arrangement should be sustained and that the presidency should remain in Southern Nigeria in the next electoral cycle, in line with the spirit of power rotation that has helped preserve peace and stability in the country.” The monarchs explained that their position was informed by the need to strengthen mutual trust among the federating units and preserve the delicate balance required for the country’s continued progress. They added that the position was intended to promote “national balance, mutual trust among the federating units, and the continued progress of the Nigerian State”. On the 2027 general elections, the traditional rulers called on political parties, candidates and the electorate to embrace democratic values and shun activities capable of undermining the electoral process. They condemned electoral violence, intimidation, vote-buying and other forms of electoral malpractice, emphasising the need for peaceful, free and credible elections at all levels. “The Council underscored the importance of peaceful, free, and credible elections at all levels. item.title: 2027: SDP inaugurates 12,000-member campaign council, names Tanko coordinator
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) has inaugurated a 12,000-member Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, with Dr Yunusa Tanko appointed as its National Coordinator. The SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, who will also serve as chairman of the council, inaugurated the campaign council on Wednesday in Abuja. Gombe charged members of the council to work towards securing electoral victory for the party, stressing that its campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and guided by the provisions of the Constitution, the Electoral Act, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) guidelines and the party’s constitution. He urged members to approach the election with the seriousness it deserved, adding that the party was determined to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “Let us approach this election with the seriousness it deserves to unseat President Tinubu. “Our campaign must be issue-based, people-centred and firmly rooted in the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the Electoral Act, INEC guidelines and our party constitution. “We must earn the confidence of Nigerians through credible engagement, persuasion, effective organisation and practical policy alternatives. “We must reject violence, intimidation, electoral malpractice and every conduct capable of undermining the integrity of our democracy,” he said. The SDP chairman described Nigeria as being at a critical crossroads, citing insecurity, economic hardship, unemployment, poverty, institutional weaknesses and declining public confidence in governance as some of the challenges confronting the country. According to him, Nigerians are yearning for purposeful leadership, economic opportunities, social justice, security and accountability, as well as a government that prioritises their welfare and dignity. He said the SDP was determined to provide Nigerians with a credible democratic alternative founded on social justice, equity, freedom, inclusive development and good governance. Gombe urged members of the campaign council to take the party’s message to communities across the country, engage citizens respectfully, listen to their concerns and demonstrate through their conduct that the party deserved their confidence. He further charged the council to ensure that the party’s campaign remained peaceful, credible and focused on offering practical solutions to the country’s challenges. item.title: Obi prefers ‘anywhere food is ready politics’ – Wike
item.description: Says, Atiku won’t get 25% across South By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Mr Peter Obi, prefers “anywhere food is ready politics”. Wike spoke on Tuesday when he met youth stakeholders in the FCT to campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election. “Obi is not going anywhere. Don’t deceive yourself. If he likes, let him enter the motorcycle and carry everybody at the back; he is not going anywhere,” the minister said. He mocked Obi’s visits to camps for internally displaced persons (IDPs). ” He goes to IDP camp to do birthdays. When he was governor, did he do that? No. Very soon, they will start going along the trees, buying and chewing corn. “He prefers anywhere Mama Put is ready for politics. He doesn’t want to struggle. Small fight, he ran away from the PDP. He did the same in the Labour Party, and now he is in NDC. But, as for me, I am not afraid of fighting. They have now run away from the PDP, and I am still in the party,” he said. The minister also dismissed the chances of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress ADC presidential candidate. “Atiku won’t get 25 per cent in South South, South East and South West. Where will he get it?” he asked. He urged the youths to do more than vote for Tinubu. “Please, I beg of you, not to just come out to vote, not to just endorse this president here, mobilise all your colleagues, even those who are not part of your association, reach out to them, and get everybody to come out. “I am not a member of the All Progressives Congress. You don’t need to be an APC member or a Peoples Democratic Party PDP member for you to contribute to the development of your country. All you need to do is to work according to the vision of the person who has appointed you. Let’s not put our destiny in the hands of political gamblers who have been gambling for over 22 years,” he said. Wike reminded the youths of the record of earlier administrations on their welfare and that of women in the FCT. “Atiku Abubakar was vice president from 1999 to 2007. Is it not correct? Correct. Was there any establishment of a youth secretariat? No. Was there any establishment of a women’s secretariat? No. From 1976 to 2023, nobody cared,” he added. He said Tinubu changed that within a year of taking office. “Go and make sure there is a youth secretary. Go and make sure there’s a woman secretary,” he quoted the president as directing. He urged the youths to ignore showmanship. “Leave all these rhetorics; leave all this drama. These are cosmetic. Let us face the reality on the ground. That is what matters,” he said. item.title: Kerrygold Engages Women in Business and Leadership at 25th WIMBIZ Annual Conference
item.description: Kerrygold, the renowned Irish dairy brand from Ornua, strengthened its engagement with consumers at the 25th Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) Annual Conference, held on November 5 and 6, 2026, at Eko Hotel & Suites, Lagos. The conference, which marked 25 years of WIMBIZ’s commitment to empowering women, brought together business leaders, entrepreneurs, professionals and public sector executives for conversations around leadership, enterprise development and the evolving role of women in business. This year’s edition was themed “Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World.” As a sponsor of the conference, Kerrygold leveraged the platform to increase brand visibility, deepen consumer engagement and strengthen its relevance among an audience of accomplished and influential women. A key feature of its participation was an exhibition stand where attendees had the opportunity to discover the brand, learn more about its product offerings and sample its products. The activation provided an opportunity for direct interaction with consumers, allowing guests to experience Kerrygold firsthand while creating meaningful brand touchpoints beyond traditional brand visibility. Through these engagements, Kerrygold reinforced its commitment to bringing its quality dairy products closer to consumers and building lasting relationships through relevant experiences. Commenting on the brand’s participation, Titilayo Ijiyokunola, General Manager, Ornua Dairy Products Nigeria Ltd., said: “At Kerrygold, we recognise the important role women play in shaping businesses, industries and communities. Our participation at WIMBIZ provides an opportunity to connect with this community, recognise their contributions and support platforms that champion leadership, enterprise and professional growth.” Kerrygold’s participation at the conference reflects its continued interest in engaging consumers through platforms that bring people together, create opportunities for meaningful interactions and allow more people to experience the quality and distinctive offerings of the brand. About Kerrygold Kerrygold is a globally trusted Irish dairy brand renowned for its quality, rich taste and provenance. Built on generations of dairy knowledge and heritage, Kerrygold is made with the finest milk from grass-fed cows and quality ingredients, with no artificial ingredients. In Nigeria, Kerrygold Milk is manufactured and distributed by Ornua Nigeria, bringing the brand’s distinctive rich, creamy taste and heritage to consumers across the country. item.title: ADC to EFCC, INEC: Probe alleged cash, gift distribution by APC officials
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to investigate alleged distribution of cash and gifts by All Progressives Congress (APC) officials at political events. The party urged the two agencies to examine the reported incidents and publicly disclose the steps being taken to address any possible violations of electoral and currency laws. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, accused the ruling party of attempting to manufacture support for President Bola Tinubu through financial inducements. The call followed the circulation of a video showing the Minister of Women Affairs and Social Development, Imaan Sulaiman-Ibrahim, distributing bundles of cash and APC-branded wrappers to women at a political gathering in Rivers State. The 45-second video, shared on TikTok by Move with Imaan, an account documenting the minister’s activities, showed Sulaiman-Ibrahim handing out bundles of cash and a bale of wrappers bearing the APC logo to women at the gathering. The video also showed her distributing cash in envelopes bearing the images of Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima, with recipients appearing to receive bundles of N1,000 notes. ‘Pattern becoming impossible to ignore’ Reacting to the development, Shaibu alleged that the distribution of money and gifts at political gatherings was an attempt to buy public support amid prevailing economic hardship. “The pattern is becoming impossible to ignore. From reports of luxury vehicles presented to APC women leaders, to cash and cooked food distributed by the President’s son through the City Boy Movement, and now videos circulating of an APC women leader handing out money and fabrics, the ruling party appears to be treating political support as something that can be bought,” he said. The ADC spokesperson described the alleged distributions as particularly insensitive at a time when millions of Nigerians were struggling to afford food, transportation and other basic necessities. He also questioned why ordinary Nigerians had faced sanctions over alleged abuse of the naira while political operatives appeared to be distributing cash at campaign events. “The same authorities that have pursued ordinary Nigerians over alleged abuse of the Naira must explain why apparent cash distribution by political operatives at campaign events should be treated differently,” he said. “The EFCC and INEC must investigate these incidents and take appropriate action wherever electoral or currency laws have been breached.” Shaibu also accused the Tinubu administration of worsening economic hardship, rising insecurity and public debt, arguing that cash and gifts could not erase the difficulties confronting Nigerian households. “After three and a half years of economic hardship, rising insecurity and mounting public debt, the

item.title: Nigeria’s crude oil output drops to 1.51m bpd in October — NUPRC
item.description: Nigeria’s crude oil production declined slightly to 1.51 million barrels per day (bpd) in October 2026, from 1.53 million bpd recorded in September, according to data from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC). The figure represents a 1.7 per cent month-on-month decline. Despite the drop, Nigeria maintained crude oil production above its Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) quota of 1.5 million bpd for the sixth consecutive month in 2026. OPEC data showed that Nigeria produced 1.5 million bpd in August, 1.50 million bpd in July, 1.55 million bpd in June and 1.53 million bpd in May. When condensates are included, the country’s average daily production stood at 1.68 million barrels in October. NUPRC data also showed that daily production peaked at 1.79 million barrels during the month, while the lowest output was 1.60 million barrels per day. The commission attributed the relatively stable production levels in recent months to improved operational stability, production uptime and crude evacuation efficiency. “The sustained growth recorded in October reflects the continued commitment of operators and industry stakeholders towards improving operational efficiency, maintaining asset integrity, and enhancing production reliability across the Nigerian upstream petroleum sector,” the commission said. A breakdown of daily average crude oil and condensate production by terminals and streams showed that Forcados recorded the highest output at 318,490 barrels per day, followed by Bonny Terminal with 311,020 bpd. Qua Iboe Terminal recorded an average production of 173,970 bpd, while Escravos Oil Terminal posted a daily average of 134,670 bpd. The commission added that Bonga ranked as the fifth-highest producing terminal, recording an average of 106,650 bpd of crude oil and condensate. item.title: Reps seek emergency funding for teaching hospitals as health budget falls to 4.2%
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to urgently increase funding for federal teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, the National Hospital Abuja and other tertiary health institutions, warning that inadequate resources are undermining specialist healthcare delivery across the country. The lawmakers also urged the government to establish a dedicated infrastructure revitalisation programme, improve the welfare of healthcare workers and ensure timely release of approved funds to the institutions. The resolutions followed a motion of urgent public importance moved by Rep. Patrick Umoh during Wednesday’s plenary, in which he drew attention to declining health budget allocations, deteriorating infrastructure, inadequate medical equipment and the continued migration of doctors, nurses and other skilled professionals. Presenting the motion, Umoh said federal tertiary health institutions remained central to specialist medical services, healthcare training and research but were struggling with dilapidated facilities, insufficient bed spaces, unreliable electricity supply and rising operational costs. He said urgent legislative intervention was necessary to strengthen the institutions and ensure that Nigerians had access to quality, affordable and accessible specialist healthcare. The lawmaker also commended the Federal Government for its continued interest in and prioritisation of the health sector. However, he expressed concern that Nigeria’s health sector allocation remained significantly below the 15 per cent commitment made by African governments under the 2001 Abuja Declaration. According to the motion, the proposed federal health budget allocation declined from approximately 5.33 per cent in 2023 to 4.20 per cent in the proposed 2026 budget. Umoh also cited figures indicating that only 30 per cent of the health sector’s 2023 capital appropriation was released, while approximately 15.06 per cent of the 2024 capital allocation was reportedly released and utilised. The motion further stated that only N36 million was reportedly released from the N218 billion appropriated for the Ministry of Health’s 2025 capital expenditure. The lawmaker warned that inadequate funding had contributed to overcrowded hospitals, delays in treatment, poor maintenance of facilities and shortages of essential medical equipment, forcing some patients to seek treatment in private hospitals or abroad. He also linked the growing migration of doctors, consultants and nurses to the declining capacity of public tertiary hospitals to provide specialist services. Umoh said the recently reported Ebola case in Nigeria had further underscored the need to strengthen the country’s tertiary health institutions and their capacity to respond to public health emergencies. item.title: Tinubu recycling failed 2023 promises in 2027 manifesto, says ADC
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has accused President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress, APC, of recycling unfulfilled 2023 campaign promises in their newly unveiled 2027 manifesto, challenging the President to account for his record before seeking another mandate. The party said the manifesto reads like the programme of a political party seeking power for the first time, rather than that of a government that has controlled the Federal Government for nearly 12 years and has had more than three years under Tinubu to deliver on its promises. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC cited healthcare coverage, ICT job creation and electricity generation as examples of promises it said the administration had failed to fulfil, questioning why Nigerians should be asked to embrace another set of commitments without an account of the previous ones. “The fundamental question Nigerians must ask is simple: Why is a government campaigning on promises it should already have fulfilled? President Tinubu has been in office since May 2023. The APC has controlled the Federal Government for nearly twelve years. Yet, reading this manifesto, one would think they are only now discovering the problems they were elected to solve,” the ADC said. The party recalled that Tinubu had promised in 2023 to extend health insurance coverage to 40 per cent of Nigerians within two years and create one million ICT jobs within 24 months. It claimed that barely one in ten Nigerians was now covered by health insurance, while government figures indicated that only about 15,000 jobs and opportunity pathways had been recorded, with the health insurance target shifted to 2031. The ADC also questioned the administration’s electricity performance, pointing out that the APC had described 4,500 megawatts of power generation as a crisis in 2023, only for its new manifesto to acknowledge average generation of 4,022 megawatts. “How does a government campaign to solve a crisis it has made remarkably worse?” the party queried. The opposition party further faulted Tinubu’s promise to introduce a programme for his first 100 days after re-election, arguing that the president already had the executive powers to implement the proposed measures without waiting for another electoral victory. “Most astonishingly, President Tinubu now promises a programme for his first 100 days after re-election, including measures he already possesses the executive powers to implement right now. What exactly is stopping him from acting today? What stopped him from acting in 2023 when he came into office?” the ADC asked. item.title: Soludo celebrates Anambra-born U-17 Golden Ball winner, Umejiaku
item.description: By Steve Oko Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, has celebrated Oluebube Umejiaku, the Anambra-born midfielder who emerged the Most Valuable Player at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Umejiaku won the prestigious Golden Ball award after inspiring Nigeria’s Flamingos to a historic 2-1 victory over Japan in the final played on November 7. The talented midfielder also scored Nigeria’s decisive second goal, sealing the victory and earning the Player of the Match award in the final. The triumph marked the first time an African women’s national team had won a FIFA World Cup title at any level. Soludo, through his Chief Press Secretary, Christian Aburime, described Umejiaku’s performance at the tournament as superlative. In recognition of her achievement, the Chairman of the Anambra State Football Association, General Chikelue Iloenyosi, travelled to Abuja on November 9 to receive and celebrate the young football star on behalf of the state government. Iloenyosi commended Soludo for his commitment to sports development and efforts to identify and nurture sporting talents across the state. He said Umejiaku’s emergence on the global stage underscored the importance of grassroots sports development and sustained investment in young talents. The Golden Ball winner’s achievement has also been described as a major source of inspiration to aspiring female footballers in Anambra State and the South-East. From her early football development to becoming the standout player at a global tournament, Umejiaku’s rise represents a significant milestone for women’s football in the state. Her performance in Morocco has further highlighted Nigeria’s potential in women’s youth football and placed her among the emerging talents attracting attention on the global stage. item.title: 2027: IGP Disu warns police against partisan politics
item.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has warned police officers against partisan political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that the Nigeria Police Force must remain neutral and loyal to the Constitution. Disu gave the warning on Wednesday while addressing senior police officers, including Deputy Inspectors-General of Police, zonal Assistant Inspectors-General and Commissioners of Police, at the monthly meeting of the Goodluck Ebele Peacekeeping Centre. He said the police had a responsibility to provide a safe and secure environment for all electoral participants, irrespective of their political affiliations. The IGP warned that he would not tolerate any officer using the authority of the police to advance the interests of political parties, candidates or their sponsors. He said officers found colluding with political actors, facilitating thuggery, compromising the electoral process or interfering with voters’ rights would face disciplinary action in accordance with the law. “As we approach another important electoral period, I wish to emphasise that it is our responsibility to guarantee a safe and secure environment for all electoral participants, irrespective of their political affiliation. “Every candidate, political party, supporter and eligible voter is entitled to equal protection under the law,” he said. Disu directed Commissioners of Police to commence comprehensive preparations for election security in their respective commands. He ordered the immediate cancellation of leave for officers and personnel assigned to election security duties, adding that Commissioners of Police and other senior officers must remain in their respective commands until the conclusion of the electoral process. He said any travel outside their commands would require express approval from Force Headquarters. The IGP also directed commands to verify their election security equipment, communication systems, operational vehicles and protective gear and report their readiness by the end of the week. He instructed Commissioners of Police to establish direct coordination with the Independent National Electoral Commission, military, Department of State Services and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in their respective states. According to him, the police remain the lead agency for election security and must demonstrate effective coordination with other security agencies. He further directed every command to submit daily situation reports to Force Headquarters throughout the electoral period, with the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations coordinating the reports and briefing him every morning. item.title: Senate passes bill to reform senior secondary education
item.description: By Henry Umoru The Senate has passed the National Senior Secondary Education Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeking to strengthen the administration, coordination and governance of public senior secondary education in Nigeria. The executive bill, sponsored by President Bola Tinubu, was transmitted to the Senate in July 2026 for legislative consideration. The proposed legislation, titled the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (SB. 1075), was passed on Wednesday after consideration of the report of the Senate Committee on Education (Basic and Secondary). Senator Orji Uzor Kalu (APC, Abia North) presented the committee’s report on behalf of its chairman, Senator Lawal Adamu Usman (Kaduna Central). Following a clause-by-clause consideration of the report at the Committee of the Whole, the Senate approved the bill, which was subsequently read for the third time and passed. Presenting the report, Kalu urged the Senate to consider and adopt the recommendations of the committee on the proposed legislation. According to the report, the National Senior Secondary Education Commission was established under the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act, 2023, to regulate and promote the development of senior secondary education in Nigeria. It stated that experience gained in implementing the Act had revealed areas requiring amendments to strengthen governance, improve coordination between the Federal and State Governments, promote accountability and support the effective implementation of national education policies. The report added that the proposed amendments were intended to address the identified challenges and make the legislation more effective in achieving its objectives. Kalu disclosed that the House of Representatives had also considered the bill and referred it to its Committee on Basic Education and Services for further legislative action. He said this informed the decision to conduct a joint stakeholder hearing and clause-by-clause consideration to ensure comprehensive consolidation, a uniform report and smoother legislative proceedings. Recall that President Tinubu transmitted the executive bill to the Senate in July through a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary. In the letter, Tinubu said the Federal Executive Council had approved the amendment bill at its meeting on April 30, 2026, before the Federal Ministry of Justice vetted and finalised it in line with constitutional provisions and legislative drafting standards. The President said the proposed amendment was part of his administration’s commitment to strengthening educational institutions in the national interest. Following the presentation of the bill, Akpabio referred it to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative processing and directed it to report back within one week. item.title: 2027: Only Yari, Alake, Idris can speak for Tinubu campaign, APC-PCC declares
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has restricted the right to speak on its behalf to three persons, ordering that everyone previously announced in that role be dissolved into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members. The Chief of Staff to the President and Deputy Director-General (Administration) of the Council, Femi Gbajabiamila, announced the changes in a statement issued on Wednesday, titled “Reorganization of Media and Communications Structure”. According to the statement, “The Council has approved that only the campaign’s Director General, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, as official Spokesperson; and the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, will speak on behalf of the Council.” Gbajabiamila said the Council made the changes “to ensure more cohesive, disciplined, and effective public engagement”. He said that “all previously announced persons in this capacity shall henceforth dissolve into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members.” The statement also put broadcasters on notice. Radio and television stations were advised “to take note of these changes and act accordingly”. item.title: 2027: Obi is desperate, not wired for long-term solutions — Oshiomhole
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senator Adams Oshiomhole has accused Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi of focusing on importation rather than job creation and long-term solutions, alleging that his promise to serve only four years reflects desperation to become president. Oshiomhole made the remarks while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday. Framing the 2027 election as a choice about Nigeria’s future, he urged young voters to back Tinubu and contrasted what he described as the President’s long-term development agenda and plans to improve the power sector with Obi’s business record and four-year pledge. Addressing young Nigerians, the APC chieftain urged students, graduates and young workers to compare the time it takes industrialists such as Aliko Dangote to establish factories and create jobs with what he described as Obi’s focus on setting up shopping malls. “That said, I need to talk to us, you young people. What this election is about is you. You as students, some of you are graduates, some of you are young workers. You talk to Dangote and ask him how long does it take him to set up a factory, to set up a refinery that today employs 10s of 1000s of workers. Then go and ask Obi how long it takes him to set up a shopping mall. To set up a shopping mall, you need short-term funds, and that is the logic of Peter Obi,” he said. Oshiomhole alleged that Obi was not inclined to develop long-term solutions that could produce sustainable growth. He also questioned Obi’s business record, asking why an unemployed person should accept advice on job creation from someone he accused of selling imported products instead of locally made Yoruba Adire. “He cannot; he’s not wired to think of long-term solutions that produce sustainable growth and development. Another one: if there is anybody who is unemployed, ask Obi, why are you selling imported products?” Oshiomhole asked. He further argued that a person whose main business was importation could not credibly lecture Nigerians on job creation, and described Obi’s pledge to serve for four years as evidence of what he called desperation. “So, anyone whose main business is importation cannot lecture us about job creation because he doesn’t mean it. And for you to see the desperation, he will say he will do four years. So he is a man who just wants it to be said that once upon a time there was a Peter in the villa. Nigeria needs statesmen, not petty traders in politics,” he added. Turning to Tinubu’s re-election bid, Oshiomhole said the President knew the need to increase the purchasing power of poorer Nigerians and create jobs. item.title: VIDEO: Tinubu Receives Flamingos In Abuja After World Cup Victory
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has received the Flamingos after winning Africa’s first-ever U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, received the victorious players and technical crew on behalf of the President at the Presidential Banquet Hall, Abuja. ﻿ The U-17 team won their first FIFA World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos lost their opener 2-1 to Poland, but dominated in the remaining matches, defeating defending champions North Korea, Puerto Rico, and Mexico. Their first-ever appearance in the final was sealed with a 3-1 victory over Brazil, before taking home the trophy after beating Japan. Flamingos celebrating their U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup The players have received commendations from government officials and football fans around the world. President Tinubu congratulated the Flamingos for becoming the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, said he received the news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States. He also described Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the country and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. The Senate also pledged a ₦100 million reward for the Flamingos. The pledge followed a motion moved by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi, who congratulated the players on their outstanding performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) for its role in the team’s achievement. The latest feat by a Nigerian sports team came less than two years after the senior women’s football team, Super Falcons, won their 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in Morocco. item.title: Many terrorists neutralised as military sustains pressure on enclaves
item.description: Scores of terrorists have been neutralised across different communities in the Northern region of the country following the pressure sustained in their enclaves by the troops of the Nigerian military. The troops, in different operations sustained pressure on the criminals and dismantled criminal networks with a view to protecting lives and property, and restoring lasting peace and security across the country. Daily Trust reports that the development was in line with the commitment of the Armed Forces of Nigeria under the leadership of General Olufemi Olatunbosun Oluyede. The four-star general, has at different fora maintained that he would continue to ensure that all law-abiding Nigerians, particularly those in the Northern Nigeria sleep with their two eyes closed. Updating Nigerians on the efforts being made to restore peace across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja disclosed that consistent efforts were made to deny terrorists, kidnappers, gunrunners and other criminal groups’ freedom of action between October 30th and November 5th, 2026. Terrorists suffer heavy losses in Northeast Checks showed that in the North East geopolitical zone, troops of Operation HADIN KAI inflicted heavy losses on terrorists who attempted to strike at troops’ locations in Borno and Yobe States. Subsequently, troops pressed home the advantage with clearance operations and a wave of arrests. On the night of October 29th, 2026, terrorists approached Buni Yadi in Gujba LGA of Yobe State, from the Timbuktu Triangle axis. However, troops countered the attack and subsequent exploitation on 30 October 30th, 2026 discovered the bodies of 48 terrorists, along with 42 AK-47 rifles, five PKT machine guns, four general-purpose machine guns, a 60mm mortar, 105 magazines and two video cameras. The following day, troops’ operations around Apama and Jauro Bashir along the terrorists’ withdrawal route, recovered three corpses, an AK-47 rifle and 188 rounds of ammunition. The senior military officer confirmed that on the same day, terrorists also attempted to infiltrate a troops’ location at Bitta in Gwoza LGA of Borno State but were forced to retreat. He added, “Exploitation at first light recovered the bodies of seven terrorists, four AK-47 rifles, an RPG tube, four RPG bombs, three RPG chargers, a PKM machine gun and a radio. “Troops also received several surrendered members of terrorist groups, rescued escapees and dismantled terrorist support networks across the theatre. “Between 2 – 4 November 2026, twelve terrorist fighters and family members surrendered at New Abaram Resettlement Village and Banki Junction in Bama LGA and near Ngurusoye in Gwoza LGA in Borno State.” On November 2nd, 2026, troops rescued a female abductee who had escaped from the Mandara Mountains at Hudugum, Hambagda, along the Gwoza-Limankara Road.
